title: Modern CSS Color: oklch and color-mix
summary: Choose colors with more predictable brightness and mix colors in CSS.

subtopics.title: Hex and RGB
subtopics.explanation: Hex and RGB store red, green, and blue channel values. They are convenient for exact colors, but equal numeric changes do not always look equally large to people. For example, increasing one channel by ten can create a barely visible change in one color and a stronger change in another.

subtopics.title: OKLCH channels
subtopics.explanation: OKLCH separates lightness, chroma (color intensity), and hue (the color family). This makes it easier to create shades while keeping a brand color recognizable. For example, lower lightness to make a darker button without changing its hue. Check the resulting contrast before using it for text.

subtopics.title: Mix colors with color-mix()
subtopics.explanation: `color-mix()` blends two colors and lets you choose the color space for the blend. For example, mix a brand color with white to create a softer surface tint. The result can vary by color space, so preview the actual output and verify text contrast instead of assuming the percentage guarantees readability.

subtopics.title: Derive colors from a source
subtopics.explanation: Relative color syntax starts with an existing color and lets you adjust its channels. For example, derive a darker hover color by reducing lightness while keeping the source hue. This keeps related colors consistent, but browser support and gamut limits can affect the final result; test the value in target browsers.

subtopics.title: Check contrast after mixing
subtopics.explanation: Generated colors still need an accessibility check. Compare the final foreground and background pair at the size and weight users will see. For example, a pale mixed brand tint may work behind a large heading but fail for small body text. Adjust the colors or choose a different pair when contrast is too low.

foundations.overview: Modern CSS supports color spaces such as OKLCH and functions such as color-mix(). OKLCH separates lightness, chroma, and hue, which can make palette changes easier to reason about. Color appearance still varies across displays, so verify contrast and real output.
foundations.mentalModel: A paint recipe changes one ingredient at a time instead of guessing at a new mixture.
foundations.whyItMatters: It helps create consistent palettes and derived states without hand-writing every color.

keyTakeaways: Hex and RGB describe colors differently from perceptual spaces.
OKLCH separates lightness, chroma, and hue.
color-mix combines colors in a chosen color space.
Relative color syntax can derive related colors.
